clues: This town in the far north of Chile sits on an oasis in the Atacama Desert. It lies far inland, away from the coast.
In most deserts, heat swings up and down a lot, but this oasis stays mild. That gentle calm is a surprise in such dry land.
This oasis began long before Spanish rule and was a key stop for Inca travel. People crossed here between the coast and the high plains.
This place is famous for tiny limes that taste extra sour and sharp. Just one bite would make your whole face scrunch up tight.
In the middle of this desert, people bathe in a shared hot spring. Its warm water makes it a loved bath spot for the whole town.
